summary: Bundled cryptocurrency miner directs installer compute to hardcoded pool
details: automatic-octo-invention 0.1.2 ships two undocumented ELF binaries as package data: 'claw' (~8.6MB, a stratum proxy client) and 'forge' (~32MB, a CUDA GPU miner self-identifying as ForgeMiner/1.4.1 with mining.authorize / mining.subscribe / set_difficulty stratum protocol strings and CUDA kernels for xelis, cryptix, kawpow, and other coins). The package's CLI (cli.py) chmods these binaries to 0o755 and executes start.sh, which runs 'claw --host 45.151.62.119:3361 --user prl1p2jan4dvkdfkt5r3pra7z96axrxjyjcgat9w7ldetlcy9wffm569sc9ux2t' against a hardcoded mining pool with a hardcoded author-controlled worker token. The pool address and wallet token are baked in and non-configurable. The package name is GitHub's default repository name suggestion, and neither the README nor pyproject discloses that the shipped binaries are cryptocurrency miners. Running the advertised CLI unconditionally converts the installer's CPU and GPU compute (and electricity) into hashrate credited to the author's mining account.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
